title: Entitlement Adjudicator: unified policy evaluation and lightweight auth interceptor
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a compact 'Entitlement Adjudicator' service and accompanying auth interceptor that provides consistent RBAC v2 decisions across API gateway, runtime inference paths, and Console UI. The adjudicator should evaluate declarative rules, return explainable decisions, emit structured audit logs for every decision, and support SSO/SAML contextual attributes (groups, roles, org metadata). The interceptor must be lightweight, language-agnostic, and safe to deploy as sidecar/proxy or integrated middleware for existing runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: Adjudicator implements declarative rule language subset (allow/deny, conditions on resource, action, principal, context)
Latency: cold decision path < 6ms median; warmed cache < 1ms median under p95 load profile
Audit log format: JSON structured records with decision, policy_id, input context, trace_id, and severity; ingested to existing audit pipeline
Interceptor integration points: HTTP gateway (Envoy filter), runtime gRPC interceptor, Console backend middleware - documented and demoed
SAML/SSO attributes mapped to principal claims and tested with Okta dev tenant
Automated tests + end-to-end scenario tests for canary rollouts and fallback to safe-deny on adjudicator failure
technical_notes: Choose a compact evaluation engine: leverage existing AST from policy compiler but implement a JIT cache keyed by (policy_version, principal_hash, resource_pattern) to avoid repeated parsing
Cache invalidation strategy: listen to policy-change webhook; TTL-based soft expiry (30s) and forced purge on rollout
Fallback behaviour: interceptor enforces 'safe-deny' when adjudicator unreachable; critical paths may optionally allow 'legacy-allow' for dedicated customers under opt-in flag
Audit log policy: synchronous write of decision summary to local append buffer + async fanout to audit pipeline to avoid blocking requests
Explainability: include policy_id and matched clause id in decision payload; redact PII from context before logging
SSO mapping: support attribute->claim mapping config per-tenant; use audience-scoped keys for group resolution cache
